source_text:
Οἱ λειτουργοὶ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου περὶ μετανοίας ἐλάλησαν.
καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ δεσπότης τῶν ἁπάντων περὶ μετανοίας ἐλάλησεν μετὰ ὅρκου: Ζῶ γὰρ ἐγώ, λέγει κύριος, οὐ βούλομαι τὸν θάνατον τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ ὡς τὴν μετάνοιαν, προστιθεὶς καὶ γνώμην ἀγαθήν:
Μετανοήσατε, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ, ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνομίας ὑμῶν: εἶπον τοῖς υἱοῖς τοῦ λαοῦ μου. Ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν πυρρότεραι κόκκου καὶ μελανώτεραι σάκκου, καὶ ἐπιστραφῆτε πρός με ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ εἴπητε: Πάτερ: ἐπακούσομαι ὑμῶν ὡς λαοῦ ἁγίου.
καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ τόπῳ λέγει οὕτως: Λούσασθε καὶ καθαροὶ γένεσθε, ἀφέλεσθε τὰς πονηρίας ἀπὸ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν μου: παύσασθε ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν, μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν, ἐκζητήσατε κρίσιν, ῥύσασθε ἀδικούμενον, κρίνατε ὀρφανῷ καὶ δικαιώσατε χήρᾳ: καὶ δεῦτε καὶ διελεγχθῶμεν, λέγει κύριος: καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡς χιόνα λευκανῶ: ἐὰν δὲ ὦσιν ὡς κόκκινον, ὡς ἔριον λευκανῶ: καὶ ἐὰν θέλητε καὶ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ θέλητε μηδὲ εἰσακούσητέ μου, μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται: τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησεν ταῦτα.
πάντας οὖν τοὺς ἀγαπητοὺς αὐτοῦ βουλόμενος μετανοίας μετασχεῖν ἐστήριξεν τῷ παντοκρατορικῷ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ.
orientation: The Roman church is citing Scripture to show that God has always offered repentance, now quoting the ministers of grace and the Master himself speaking with an oath.
pass_a_gloss: The ministers of the grace of God through [the] holy Spirit about repentance spoke. And he himself, the Master of all things, about repentance spoke with an oath: For I live, says [the] Lord, I do not wish the death of the sinner as [I wish] the repentance, adding also a good counsel: Repent, house of Israel, from your lawlessness: I said to the sons of my people. If your sins are from the earth to the heaven and if they are redder than scarlet and blacker than sackcloth, and you turn to me from [the] whole heart and say: Father: I will hear you as a holy people. And in another place he says thus: Wash and become clean, remove the wickednesses from your souls before my eyes: cease from your wickednesses, learn to do good, seek out judgment, rescue [the] wronged, judge [the] orphan and justify [the] widow: and come and let us reason together, says [the] Lord: and if your sins are as crimson, as snow I will whiten [them]: and if they are as scarlet, as wool I will whiten [them]: and if you are willing and listen to me, the good things of the earth you will eat: but if you are not willing nor listen to me, a sword will devour you: for the mouth of [the] Lord has spoken these things. All his beloved ones therefore, wishing [them] to share in repentance, he established by his all-powerful will.

choices.why: The infinitive μετασχεῖν means to have a share in or partake of; the genitive μετανοίας is its object. 'Share in repentance' preserves the participial sense of μετασχεῖν.
The verb στηρίζω means to fix firmly, establish, or confirm. 'Established' fits the context of God securing his beloved ones in his will.
The adjective παντοκρατορικός derives from παντοκράτωρ (Almighty) and modifies βούλημα (will). 'All-powerful will' conveys the divine attribute attached to the will.
The verb διελέγχω means to argue through, debate, or reason with. The hortatory subjunctive 'let us reason together' matches the LXX Isaiah 1:18 context.
The adjective ἀγαπητός means beloved. The plural substantive 'beloved ones' preserves the noun-like use without adding a noun not in the text.

pass_b_english: The ministers of God's grace spoke about repentance through the Holy Spirit.
And the Lord of all things himself spoke about repentance with an oath: 'As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner as much as repentance.' And he added this good counsel:

'Repent, house of Israel, from your lawlessness. I said to the sons of my people: Even if your sins reach from earth to heaven, and even if they are redder than scarlet and blacker than sackcloth, if you turn to me with your whole heart and say, "Father," I will listen to you as to a holy people.'

And in another place he says this: 'Wash and become clean; remove the wickedness from your souls, away from my eyes. Stop your wicked deeds; learn to do good; seek justice; rescue the wronged; give judgment for the orphan and justice for the widow. Come now, and let us reason together, says the Lord. Even if your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow; even if they are like scarlet, I will make them white as wool. If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land; but if you are not willing and do not listen to me, a sword will devour you. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.'
So, wanting all his beloved ones to share in repentance, he established them by his all-powerful will.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker transitions and pronoun references, kept the divine quotations distinct, and smoothed the sentence flow for reading aloud without altering any claims or Scripture references.

problems.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
problems.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

problems.quote: As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner as much as repentance.
problems.why: Not a direct quote from any single canonical verse.

variants.text: As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner as much as repentance.

edits.old: And the Master of all things himself spoke about repentance with an oath:
edits.new: And the Lord of all things himself spoke about repentance with an oath:

fixed: The 'Master'/'Lord' variation was a real inconsistency; standardized to 'Lord' for the divine title.
The 'As I live...' passage is a paraphrase of Ezekiel 18:23, 32; 33:11, not a direct quote; no textual change needed since the English accurately renders the source.

last_rejected.quote: Even if your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow;
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡς χιόνα λευκανῶ:
last_rejected.why: Greek says sins are “like a palm (φοινικοῦν)”, not “crimson”. The translation changes the metaphor.
last_rejected.fix: Even if your sins are like a palm tree, I will make them white as snow;
last_rejected.ruling: φοινικοῦν here means crimson/scarlet (LXX Isaiah 1:18), parallel to κόκκινον; 'palm' would be absurd. 'Crimson' is correct.

last_rejected.quote: he established them by his all-powerful will.
last_rejected.source_quote: πάντας οὖν τοὺς ἀγαπητοὺς αὐτοῦ βουλόμενος μετανοίας μετασχεῖν ἐστήριξεν τῷ παντοκρατορικῷ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ.
last_rejected.why: The beloved are those he wants to share repentance; what he confirmed is that repentance, not the people.
last_rejected.fix: So, wanting all his beloved to share in repentance, he established it by his all-powerful will.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐστήριξεν with no explicit object; 'τοὺς ἀγαπητοὺς' is the natural object of the participle's main verb. 'established them' is a defensible reading, not a clear meaning change.
